to the arrival point and correcting itself a moment later — which would show up as a
visible round trip every time a staff member connects.

| Setting | Default | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Spawn on arrival** | on | The point of the component. |
| **Spawn on role change** | off | Being promoted should not yank someone across the map mid-conversation. |
| **Keep velocity** | off | Arriving at full speed makes players slide or fall. |

`FOSRespawn()` sends the local player back to their current role's point, for a
"return to spawn" button of your own.

---

## Under the hood

The matrix is **not synchronised**. It is baked into your prefab, identical on every
client, so it costs nothing on the network and no client can forge it. What travels stays
one integer of role per player — going from four roles to twenty costs nothing more.

The permissions are read by the Standard edition's authority, at the same single decision
point as before. Pro provides the data and the editor; it does not duplicate the security
model, which is the last thing that should ever exist in two copies.

---

## Notes

- Roles are edited **through the window only**. The arrays are bit masks: unreadable by
  hand, and a one-bit mistake gives a role that isolates instead of freezing with nothing
  to show for it.
- Translation keys are optional. Without them, the names in the matrix are used as-is.
- Quest and PC behave identically: there is no platform-specific code.


# FOS Lock Door System — Standard 2.0.1

A door players lock behind them: who is inside, do-not-disturb, anonymous mode, a
doorbell with a camera view, and passages reserved to whoever holds the key.

Requires **FOS Essentials Core 1.3.0**, **FOS Access 1.0.0**, **FOS Localization 1.0.0**,
**FOS Teleport 1.0.0** and **FOS UI Culling 1.0.0** — all four free.

Coming from version 1.0? **Read `CHANGELOG.md` first.** This release shares no class name
with it, and a prefab you have modified does not carry over on its own.

---

## Editions

```
Assets/FOS/LockDoorSystem/
└── Standard/     ← you are here
```

A **Pro** edition will sit next to this one, adding components beside the Standard ones
and talking to them through their public API. It will never replace a component on the
prefab, so upgrading will not cost you the wiring you already did.

---

## Setup

1. Drop **FOS Essentials > FOS Lock Door System > Standard > Lock Door System** into your
   scene.
2. Resize **Detection Zone** to cover the room. Keep its Collider on **Is Trigger**, and
   never disable the object — a disabled behaviour stops running and the room would look
   empty for good. You can turn its Mesh Renderer off.
3. Set the **room name** on the display. It overwrites what the texts hold in the scene,
   so edit it there rather than on the canvas.
4. For a reserved room: add an **Access List** (from FOS Access) somewhere in the scene,
   fill it, and point the lock and the passages at it.
5. Move the **teleport points** to suit the room.

One Access List serves every door in the world. Do not give each door its own — they would
each download the same list.

---

## Components

| Component | Role | Sync |
|---|---|---|
| `FOSDoorLock` | Decides: locked, do-not-disturb, anonymous | Manual |
| `FOSDoorOccupancy` | Holds who is in the room | Manual |
| `FOSDoorBell` | The "someone is at the door" episode | Events only |
| `FOSDoorDisplay` | Every text, icon and indicator | None |
| `FOSDoorPortal` | A passage, optionally reserved | None |

**Only `FOSDoorLock` decides anything.** Everything else reads it. That separation is what
lets you add a second panel, a remote indicator or your own behaviour without touching
the state: register with `FOSRegister`, expose a public parameterless method, and you are
notified on every change.

| Source | Event sent to those registered |
|---|---|
| `FOSDoorLock` | `FOSApplyDoorState`, and `FOSApplyDoorDenied` on a refusal |
| `FOSDoorOccupancy` | `FOSApplyOccupancy` |
| `FOSDoorBell` | `FOSApplyBell` |

---

## Coming from the 1.0 settings

| 1.0 | 2.0 |
|---|---|
| **VIP Room** | `Locked on start` ticked **and** `Unlock when empty` unticked |
| **Lock For All** | `Anyone can lock` |
| **Delay Seconds** | `Display seconds`, on the doorbell |
| **Anonym Length** | gone — the mask is a text you choose, the same for everyone |
| **Room Name** | on the display |
| `VIPChecker` | `FOSAccessList`, from the FOS Access pack |
| `HideSystem` | FOS UI Culling |
| `TeleportLDS` | `FOSDoorPortal`, on FOS Teleport |

---

## Translating the door

The interface of the **editor** is already translated. The texts shown **in your world**
are yours, and go in the FOS Localization table:

| Key | Holds |
|---|---|
| `lockdoor.ring.who` | The ringing message. Must contain the `{player}` token. |
| `lockdoor.list.empty` | Shown instead of the list when the room is empty. |
| `lockdoor.denied.notAllowed` | Shown to somebody without the key. |
| `lockdoor.denied.loading` | Shown while the access list has not arrived yet. |

Leave the locale manager empty and the fallback texts written in the display are used as
they are. The pack works without FOS Localization wired — it just speaks one language.

---

## How the network side works

State travels **only** through synchronised variables. A click takes ownership, writes,
serialises, and applies locally; every other client receives `OnDeserialization` and
applies the same thing. Nothing is reconstructed from an event, so a player arriving late
gets the whole state without anything being replayed for them.

Requests go the other way: a client asks the owner, and the owner checks who is really
calling before doing anything. Nobody can add, remove or ring on somebody else's behalf.

The doorbell synchronises **nothing at all**. Ringing is an event, not a state.

---

## What this is not

**The anonymous mode is cosmetic.** It hides names on the panel, identically for every
player — but any client can already list everyone in the instance, so it keeps nothing
secret from someone determined. It is a courtesy, not a protection.

**Access is decided on the player's own client**, as everything in Udon is. A modified
client can answer what it likes. This tidies a world; it does not guard it.

Both limits are real, and neither has a fix available in Udon. Design your world knowing
them rather than around them.

---

French Oasis Studio SAS — <contact@frenchoasis.studio>
